disease_label_per_paper: Hypocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis in systemic lupus erythematosus
presentation_summary: 50-year-old woman initially presented with a 3-month history of recurrent multiple urticarial rashes and wheals on the face, trunk, and back.
The lesions persisted for more than 24 hours and resolved with hyperpigmentation.
She had marked swelling of the face and lip, consistent with angioedema.
One year later she returned with malar rash, bilateral leg pitting edema, and recurrent urticaria.
Laboratory evaluation showed leukopenia, anemia, hypoalbuminemia, low C3, low C4, low CH50, low C1q, elevated anti-C1q, proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, and reduced creatinine clearance.
Skin biopsy showed polymorphonuclear leukocyte infiltration, neutrophils, and nuclear dust at small vessel walls.
Renal biopsy showed subepithelial and mesangial immune deposits compatible with membranous nephritis.
After steroid taper she had recurrence of urticaria, angioedema, conjunctivitis, and abdominal pain; prednisone and dapsone attenuated but did not completely eliminate lesions.

diagnostics.source_text_value: A high titer of antinuclear antibodies (ANA) was detected (1:640, speckled)

clinical_course.event: Antihistamine and prednisolone improved initial skin lesions.

clinical_course.event: Intravenous methylprednisolone pulse followed by high-dose oral steroid was administered, with mycophenolate mofetil and hydroxychloroquine added.
clinical_course.source_text_value: An intravenous steroid pulse (1.0 g/day×3 days) followed by a high-dose oral steroid (1 mg/kg) were administered... mycophenolate mofetil (500 mg, bid) and hydroxychloroquine were added.

clinical_course.event: Steroid taper was followed by recurrent urticaria, angioedema, conjunctivitis, and abdominal pain; prednisone and dapsone were started.
